extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, potential petitioners, patent owners, and litigants considering CBM review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on filing and litigating a Transitional Program for Covered Business Method (CBM) patent review before the PTAB, including eligibility, petition requirements, fees, timelines, evidentiary rules, and estoppel effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered business method subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM review offers a proceeding for challenging the validity of patents granted for methods and apparatuses for performing data processing or other operations used in the practice, administration, or management of a financial product or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must identify that the patent claims a covered business method (i.e., relates to financial product/service data-processing or related operations) because CBM review is limited to such subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological invention exception
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM review is not available for technological inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) will consider certain factors on a case-by-case basis in deciding whether a patent claims a technological invention that is not subject to CBM review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing / petitioner eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for CBM review of a patent may only be filed by a person who is sued or charged with infringement of that covered business method patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petitioner must show standing by noting the proceeding in which the petitioner has been sued on or charged with infringement of the patent of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: A CBM review provides an opportunity to challenge an issued covered business method patent on any ground, subject to certain limitations as to the types of prior art that may be submitted in a CBM review proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CBM procedure expands the grounds for unpatentability that can be alleged compared to some other proceedings, but specific limits apply to what prior art may be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on prior art submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: There are certain limitations as to the types of prior art that may be submitted in a CBM review proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes limits exist but does not list them; practitioners should consult implementing rules or PTAB guidance for specifics on allowable prior art in CBM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary program / sunset date
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM review is a temporary procedure that is set to sunset on September 16, 2020, where no additional petitions for CBM review will be accepted after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing matters: petitions must be filed before the statutory/program sunset; verify any extensions or statutory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The base filing fee for a CBM review petition is $12,000. A base institution fee of $18,000 is due if the PTAB institutes a full review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgeting for CBM includes both the initial petition filing fee and potential institution fees if PTAB institutes review; other fees/fee adjustments may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and appeal path
rubrics_metrics.description: CBM review proceedings are administrated directly by the PTAB and are heard by a panel of administrative law judges who make rulings regarding institution, discovery matters, and issuing a final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any party dissatisfied with the final written decision may appeal directly to the Federal Circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required petition content
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition for CBM review must include an identification of the real parties in interest, the claims being challenged along with explanations of grounds of unpatentability for those claims, copies of evidence relied upon and an explanation of the relevance of that evidence, along with payment of a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and well-supported petitions should identify parties, pinpoint claims, articulate grounds, submit supporting evidence with relevance explanations, and include required fees to avoid procedural defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden to show CBM status
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden is on the petitioner to show that the patent is a covered business method patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must present sufficient factual and legal support in the petition to establish that the patent falls within CBM subject matter; failure to do so risks denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of declarations and testimonial evidence by petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: The requesting party may submit declarations of supporting evidence and opinions with their request for CBM review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners commonly attach affidavits/declarations and expert opinions to support grounds and relevance of evidence; these may be used for institution decisions and discovery follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on patent owner testimonial evidence at preliminary stage
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner is prohibited from filing any testimonial evidence with their preliminary response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner testimonial evidence (affidavits/declarations) is not allowed with the preliminary response but may be filed later, such as with the patent owner response if CBM review is instituted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard (likelihood of unpatentability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon review of a requesting petition and any preliminary response by the patent owner, the PTAB will determine whether it is more likely than not that at least one of the claims challenged in the petition is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'more likely than not' standard is the threshold for instituting a full CBM review; petitions should be drafted to meet that evidentiary showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue narrowing and notice of grounds at institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB may narrow issues at this time, and will provide a decision detailing the grounds of unpatentability that will be of issue in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution decision identifies which grounds/claims proceed to trial; expect potential limiting of issues and tailor subsequent strategy accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling order and timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: After initiation of a CBM review proceeding, the PTAB will issue a scheduling order that will conclude the proceeding within 12-18 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A typical scheduling order provides the patent owner with three months to perform discovery and respond; the petitioner is then given three months to perform discovery and to respond to the patent owner’s reply; a short period for motions and a requestable oral hearing may follow; final written decision issued thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery can include depositions of any witnesses that submitted affidavits or declarations with the request petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner typically has an initial discovery window (about three months) and petitioner a subsequent window; parties should expect depositions and document discovery tied to evidentiary submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner amendment opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: A response may include a contingent motion to amend the claims. This is the only opportunity that the patent owner has to amend the claims by right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners wishing to amend should use the response stage to present contingent claim amendments; other opportunities may be limited and subject to PTAB rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement during proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are permitted to settle during the proceedings, unless the PTAB has already decided on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement can terminate proceedings prior to final decision; once PTAB issues a merits decision, settlement cannot undo the final written decision's effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel effect and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel for the requesting party applies upon issuance of the final written decision by the board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The estoppel resulting from a CBM review in subsequent district court and International Trade Commission (ITC) proceedings is more limited than that of an inter partes review: estoppel extends only to grounds that the petition actually raised during the CBM review.
